sections.grading:
Grading is based on:
1) Assignments (Best 10 out of 12), 5% each, 50% total
2) Final Exam 40%
3) Attendance 10%

For 1), you can buy sources to find out the answers easily, but I suggest you to do once before using sources. If you know how to do assignment, you know how to do the final exam, the concept and question types are similar.

For 2), 11 or 13 long questions in the final as I remember, each chapter contains 1 question (if there are 2 parts then 2 questions), no question about chapters 1 and 2. The final exam questions are similar to homework, so if you want to save your time, you just need to familiar with the "practice" from Wiley course Resources, and the assignment done. Textbook exercises are too difficult and will not be tested in final exam. As you can bring 1 cheatsheet, you don't need to remember the entries.

I do not buy sources so I don't know whether the final exam paper is the same as sources.  

you have 3 hours to complete the exam, if you familiar with the questions, you should be able to complete it within 2 hours.

3) Attendance
I do not attend the lesson so  I cannot tell you how she counts it. In the first lesson, the professor said that she saw a girl watch her video and work hard in the library, so she decided to remove attendance and give everyone full marks. But from what I have heard from my friends later, the attendance score is based on your final exam result -_- (not verified so don't trust it).

My Grades:
Full for assignment
Unreleased for attendance and final exam, TA don't reply me as well.
Final grade : A-

There is only 1 question I don't know in the final exam, which is chapter 12 and not taught by the professor (you have to study by yourself before the week of examination), so I would say the exam paper is easy and grading is competitive.

sections.teaching:
The course was delivered in blended learning mode, you have to watch all videos of the specific chapter every week by yourself, and attend a lecture with Amy once a week. While Amy was pregnant this semester so we had a zoom class every week. You may send her some questions before class and she will mention them in class with all of us. It is helpful if you have questions to ask.
Amy always shares different articles and essays. You may find it interesting if you love accounting.
sections.grading:
Class participation 10%
Just attend the class and you can get it.

Graded homework 5%*10
There will be 12 homework, and only the best 10 out of 12 will be used.

Final exam 40%
One two-sided A4 cheatsheet is allowed. While you have to put everything in the 12 chapters inside. It is pretty hard since there are a lot of terms and formatting that you have to know. There will be around 13 questions in the exam, and all of them require the preparation of some statements. The exam lasts for 3 hours and I barely completed it. The exam result and statistics are not released.

As a student who only got a B in ACCT2010 and had no accounting background before, I get an A. So I believe the grading is pretty good.
sections.workload: It is pretty terrible. First, you have to spend around 2-3 hours watching the videos by yourself (which I strongly recommend you double the speed, Amy speaks kinda slow). After that, you have to do homework EVERY WEEK. It takes me a lot of time since I don't have an accounting background. I spent like 2-3 hours per homework.

sections.content:
Required textbook : Kieso, Donald E., Weygandt, Jerry J. AND Warfield, Terry D., “Intermediate Accounting: IFRS Edition, 4th Edition”, Wiley.
The textbook is also required for ACCT3020 so make sure you bought the latest version.

Chapter 1 – 2 : background of Accounting and Reporting Standards, full of texts ,not much being tested in the final exam, but they are the basis of later chapters.

Chapter 4 – 5 : Financial statements ( 4 of them, Income Statements, Statement of Financial Position, Statement of Cash Flows, and Statement of changes in equity )
Be careful about the presentation and format of these statements, about 2 -3 questions in the final exam are related to financial statements.

Chapter 6 is skipped, FINA2303 stuff  (time value of money) , present value, future value, and annuity formulas. They are essential for later chapters in calculations.

Chapter 7 : Receivables , Accounts receivables and Notes receivables , calculations of present value and interest of Notes , Secured Borrowing and Refund Liability.

Chapter 8 – 9 : Inventories , valuation issues of inventories

Chapter 10 – 11 : Valuation of PPE and depreciation calculation

Chapter 12 : Intangible assets  and impairment loss of goodwill  ( self-study part for final exam )

If you do it wrong for the first attempt, then find a friend to ask for their answers. However, the numbers for some questions maybe different as they are auto-generated. Just ask them for the formula is fine.

The final exam covers all the materials taught throughout the semester, and most of the questions are in the form of preparation of journal entries. I think it is the best to study hard for the final exam as it is the key factor that mainly affects your grade.

Not too sure how the participation score is counted. Sometimes, she will give out a piece of blank paper before the F2F class starts and requires students to write their questions on the paper. Lmao I somehow managed to get B+ given the fact that I did not watch any of her lecture videos and by just reading the textbook.

The extension of ACCT 2010. The content is relatively simple, and most knowledge is built on the topics of ACCT 2010. Therefore, revision on ACCT 2010 is very important before entering this course.

sections.teaching:
Amy mainly teaches according to powerpoints, while she tries her best to incorporate business news related to topics to make lessons more interesting.

She often ends her lessons early, as the schedule is not that tight in this semester, but her speed is quite fast during lessons. She explains some common mistakes and clarifies common misconceptions of her previous students during classes.
sections.grading: Standard grading. Amy always says that students from the Accounting department are outstanding, but she needs to distribute grades in accordance with the university policy.

sections.content:
Content was very standard. The first few classes was about the IFRS framework (which was a bit boring), and then we start talking about the asset side of the B/S (which is the focus of the whole course). Content was not difficult to digest, but we needed to memorize a lot of journal entries, so practice practice practice to understand what situation to do which entry.
There's also a project that focuses on revenue recognition to deepen our understanding of the topic, coz there was a new guideline (IFRS 15) that was just published.
sections.teaching: Amy was a very good professor, but a lot of the time she reads the PPT, and uses examples from the textbook directly. She has a deep understanding of the market, and will sometimes share her thoughts on some market news during class. But since the examples were really limited, we have to do a lot of practice to understand more. Also, this semester was the first time Amy asked students to do a project for this course, so she didn't really give clear instructions on how to complete the project. In the end, after the presentation, she commented that we should focus a bit more on the quantitative side of things (meaning we should focus on how to do journal entries instead of just explaining the new revenue recognition rules) and the market's reaction to the new rule. So next year be aware of that.
sections.grading: Standard SBM grading, 25% A. But accounting major students are all very diligent, so it may be hard to get an A.
sections.workload:
The workload for this course is higher than last year, since we have a new online homework platform and a project besides the exams. Always check Canvas for new homework postings to avoid missing deadlines. Before the exam, practice with textbook questions (ideally, finish all of them) as you will definitely come across them during the exams. This year's final exam questions were all from the textbook exercises. Exams are all non-cumulative.
After the midterm, start doing the project, instead of leaving it for the final few weeks, or you won't have much time.
